chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
that he forbade (using) vessels of gold and silver
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on using gold and silver vessels for eating and drinking?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) establishes the prohibition of using gold and silver vessels for eating and drinking, a ruling deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence to distinguish between luxury and utility. It reflects the broader ethical principle of avoiding extravagance (israf) and maintaining humility in daily consumption, as emphasized by the Ahl al-Bayt. The prohibition serves both as a legal directive and a spiritual reminder to prioritize inner purity over material opulence.
